title: Day-4 TWC tournament-card market observations
provenance: Captured by this session's own research fetch of the providers' public APIs on 2026-10-16T23:45Z-2026-10-17T00:10Z (session clock). This is a dated observation, NOT the production pipeline's collected evidence: the four-hour publisher re-collects these same public endpoints on the GitHub runner through scripts/twc_lines.py and recomputes every probability from its own retained originals. Nothing here overwrites a live line, and no value was inferred, copied from a directory percentage or taken from Hotspawn.
derivation: Provider quote arrays are stored in the fixture's own team order (the order HLTV publishes), so no reader has to re-align a provider's display order. Polymarket: quote = (best bid + best ask)/2 per outcome token from the original CLOB order book, with size>0 and a spread ceiling of 0.12. Kalshi: quote = (yes_bid + yes_ask)/2 per binary market. Each provider pair is normalized, and the published pair is the median across providers, one vote each - the same rule scripts/originate.py applies to the weekly list. Fair lines are illustrative reciprocals, not executable quotes.
limitations: Two independent providers only (Polymarket, Kalshi); this is not a broad multi-book consensus.

Kalshi traded volume on these two events is small (hundreds to about 2.8k contracts) and its published books had not moved since 17:30Z/21:40Z, so that provider contributes a thinner signal than Polymarket.
Midpoints are not guaranteed execution prices; exchange fees and rule differences are excluded.

TWC playoff fixtures are not in the weekly Hotspawn scheduled-fixture inventory, so no Hotspawn lock time exists for them; the tournament pick'em lock is not published in a verifiable form here and is therefore left blank.
Hotspawn community percentages, HLTV fan votes and tournament outright odds are not used anywhere.

Line movement shown here is limited to what the captured books prove: provider book update timestamps and the absence of a reprice. A verified point change requires the pipeline's own retained earlier read, which scripts/twc_lines.py replays and drops if its originals are gone.

underdog.reading: Aurora at 47.6% is a coin-flip side, far above the published 30% underdog floor, so taking Aurora to climb a leaderboard is defensible rather than reckless. The evidence for it is a market price, not a claim that the price is wrong: Aurora swept their Day-2 and Day-3 series 2-0 while FURIA needed three maps against Legacy, and FURIA's own IGL described an overbooked season on 15 October. None of that is quantified here and it never overrides the higher-probability side.
